Introduction and meaning
Affray. BNS restatement of IPC 159 / 160. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 159 / 160. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 194 is the rule on “Affray”. The section provides that (1) When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace, they are said to commit an affray. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 194 exists so that “Affray” has a closed legal test in Chapter XI — Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Unlawful assembly, common object, rioting, affray, and promoting enmity.

The provision in detail
194. (1) When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace, they are said to commit an affray

(2) Whoever commits an affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both

Essential ingredients
1. (1) When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace, they are said to commit an affray
2. (2) Whoever commits an affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both

examples.title: Example 1 — simple (teaching example)
examples.body: A short everyday fact pattern is tested against “Affray”. Name BNS s. 194, list the ingredients, and say which facts match. This is a teaching example — the statute does not print a numbered illustration under this heading.

examples.title: Example 2 — practical application / distinction (teaching example)
examples.body: Change one ingredient so that BNS s. 194 fails. A complex problem or motion often hinges on this subtle missing ingredient. State the failure expressly. Label this as an example, never as a reported case.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 194 (Affray) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 194 (Affray), Chapter XI — Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (1) When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace, they are said to commit an affray
   (2) (2) Whoever commits an affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 194 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 194 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

misconceptions.trap: Writing only the section number and title without analyzing ingredients or case ratio.
misconceptions.correction: An authoritative note defines the concept, lists ingredients, uses an illustration, states explanations/exceptions, applies the test, and concludes with BNS s. 194.

misconceptions.trap: Copying a statutory illustration without mapping it to an ingredient.
misconceptions.correction: Quote the illustration, then write which ingredient it proves or which ingredient is missing. Mapping is the core evidentiary link.

misconceptions.trap: Giving a one-line summary or shortened explanation of the provision.
misconceptions.correction: Authoritative chamber practice and judicial papers require a complete answer. The analysis on this page is written at full length for that reason.

Introduction. BNS s. 194 deals with Affray. It sits in Chapter XI — Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Affray. BNS restatement of IPC 159 / 160. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 159 / 160. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.

The section provides that (1) When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace, they are said to commit an affray. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. (1) When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace, they are said to commit an affray
2. (2) Whoever commits an affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Unlawful assembly, common object, rioting, affray, and promoting enmity.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Analytical comment. Explain a condition, a proviso, or a practical difficulty in applying s. 194. Do not invent case names.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 194.”

examTips: Cite BNS s. 194 for offences on or after 1 July 2024.
Ingredients first, illustration second, application third, conclusion last.
Do not cite the IPC number in a post-1 July 2024 charge-sheet unless s. 358 savings apply.

examFrameworks.question: Structured Legal Assessment: BNS s. 194 (Affray).
steps: Introduce BNS s. 194 and Chapter XI — Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity.
Define / state the meaning in your own words.
Give one labelled example and map it to an ingredient.
Apply in four to six sentences.
Conclude with the current citation — BNS s. 194.

steps: Everything in the preliminary assessment, written in full substantive depth — not summarised.
Place the section in the Chapter and explain why the heading exists.
Work a second hypothetical in which one ingredient fails.
Add analytical comment on a condition or practical difficulty.
IRAC application to the problem facts.
Address procedural hurdles, evidentiary requirements, and standard defense objections.

revisionPoints: First ingredient: (1) When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace, they are said to commit an affray
No printed illustration — prepare an original labelled example.

For offences on or after 1 July 2024, the correct citation is BNS s. 194 — Affray. Older books and judgments may still print a historical number (159 / 160). Convert it. Write the BNS number in a current answer. Do not treat the old number as if it were still the law.
